cards.name: Zoom Tool
cards.summary: Navigation tool that changes the magnification of the document window: a click zooms in around the clicked point, an Alt-click zooms out, and a drag zooms into the area you drag over. It changes only the view; artwork size, artboards and exports are untouched.
use_for: inspecting anchor points, joins and corner shapes up close before handing off a logo
checking hairlines, small type and trim marks on a print layout
framing one part of a large poster, banner or packaging dieline while editing it
avoid: resizing artwork: zoom never changes object size; use the Scale Tool or Object > Transform > Scale...
judging print size by eye at a random zoom: use View > Actual Size, or View > Fit Artboard in Window to see the whole page

selecting it from a script: the harvest probe (app.selectTool("Adobe Zoom Tool") then app.getSelectedToolName()) raised a PARM error, so tool selection is unverified; set the view's zoom and centerPoint instead
cards.how: Press Z (or pick the tool in the toolbar, where it shares a flyout slot with the Hand Tool and Rotate View Tool in the Basic toolbar). Click to zoom in centred on the click, Alt-click to zoom out. Dragging zooms to the dragged area; with animated zoom on (GPU preview) a left / right drag scrubs the zoom continuously instead. Double-clicking the tool's toolbar icon jumps to Actual Size (the same as View > Actual Size). The tool only moves the view, so it is safe to use at any time.
cards.script_api: Tool selection is unverified: in the harvest, app.getSelectedToolName() after app.selectTool("Adobe Zoom Tool") raised Error 1346458189 ('PARM'), and the batch records no invoke. The job itself is scriptable through the View object: app.activeDocument.activeView.zoom sets the zoom factor (visibleZoom is the factor the user sees) and app.activeDocument.activeView.centerPoint = [x, y] centres the view on a point; app.executeMenuCommand("zoomin") / ("zoomout") / ("actualsize") / ("fitin") run the View menu steps.

review.changes: how: '100%' (not in the batch) replaced by Actual Size / View > Actual Size; earlier adversarial pass: avoid/script_api: the PARM error is attributed as the batch states (getSelectedToolName() after selectTool()), not to selectTool alone, and selection is called unverified rather than unavailable; script_api: dropped the invented 'zoom = 4 (4 = 400%)' mapping, noted visibleZoom from the ai_api harvest

cards.name: Perspective Grid
cards.summary: Shows the document's perspective grid (one-, two- or three-point) and lets you reshape it on the canvas by dragging its widgets: vanishing points, horizon line, ground level, plane extents and grid cell size. Shapes drawn with the drawing tools while the grid is visible are drawn straight onto the active plane, so flat vector art comes out foreshortened toward the vanishing points.
use_for: packaging and product mock-ups: labels and panels on a box seen at an angle
city, street or interior illustrations built in true one-, two- or three-point perspective
signage, billboard and storefront visuals with text running along a wall
3D-feeling headline or floor typography for posters
avoid: photos and raster images: raster art does not take perspective on the grid; distort a photo in Photoshop instead (Edit > Perspective Warp or Filter > Vanishing Point)
several independent perspectives in one file: a document has one perspective grid, so build the second scene in its own document and paste the expanded result

files going to apps or print RIPs that need plain paths: type and symbols attached to the grid stay live; expand them (Object > Expand...) before handoff; shapes drawn on the grid are already ordinary paths
a quick slanted look on one object: the Free Distort effect or the Free Transform tool is faster than setting up a grid
cards.how: Press Shift+P (or pick it from the toolbar flyout it shares with Perspective Selection); the grid appears with the plane-switching widget in the corner of the window. Drag the round handles to move the left / right vanishing points, the horizon line and the ground level, drag the plane extent handles to grow or shrink each plane, and drag the grid-cell handle to change cell size. Pick a preset (one-, two- or three-point) under View > Perspective Grid, or Edit > Perspective Grid Presets... / View > Perspective Grid > Define Grid... for exact values. Click a face of the plane-switching widget to choose the active plane, then draw with the Rectangle Tool, Pen and similar tools: the shapes land on that plane in perspective. Lock the grid (View > Perspective Grid > Lock Grid) once it is set so a stray drag does not move it.
cards.script_api: app.selectTool("Perspective Grid Tool") selects the tool (verified live in the harvest), but dragging the grid widgets cannot be scripted. Document methods cover the rest: showPerspectiveGrid() / hidePerspectiveGrid(), selectPerspectivePreset(name) to switch to a preset such as "[2P-Normal View]", importPerspectiveGridPreset() / exportPerspectiveGridPreset() for custom grids saved from Define Grid, and setPerspectiveActivePlane(PerspectiveGridPlaneType.LEFTPLANE / RIGHTPLANE / FLOORPLANE / NOPLANE) before placing art.

review.changes: use_for: 'isometric-looking' removed (the grid builds perspective, not isometric projection); avoid: 'perspective art stays live' narrowed to attached type and symbols, and the wrong 'Object > ... / Create Outlines' path replaced by Object > Expand...

cards.name: Perspective Selection
cards.summary: Selection tool for the perspective grid: dragging a flat object onto the grid attaches it to the active plane (it is foreshortened to fit), and dragging, scaling or Alt-dragging objects already on a plane moves, resizes or duplicates them while keeping them in perspective. It does nothing useful while no perspective grid is shown.
use_for: putting a finished flat logo, label or poster onto the side of a box or building
sliding windows, tiles or signs along a wall so they shrink correctly toward the vanishing point
repeating fence posts, columns or floor tiles in perspective by Alt-dragging copies
resizing art that is already on a plane without breaking the perspective
avoid: ordinary selection and moving: off the grid it behaves like a clumsy Selection Tool; use the Selection Tool (V) instead
raster images, gradient meshes and envelope objects: they do not attach to a plane; keep them flat or warp them in Photoshop
editing the shape of perspective art point by point: switch to the Direct Selection tool, or release it with Object > Perspective > Release with Perspective, edit, and re-attach
type you still need to retype: it stays editable, but edit it through Object > Perspective > Edit Text rather than with the Type tool on the grid
cards.how: Show the grid (Shift+P switches to the Perspective Grid tool and shows it), then press Shift+V for Perspective Selection. Pick the target face on the plane-switching widget, drag a flat object onto the grid and release: it is attached to that plane in perspective. Drag attached objects to move them along their plane, drag bounding-box handles to scale in perspective, Alt-drag to leave a copy, and Shift-drag to constrain the move. Object > Perspective > Attach to Active Plane attaches a selection to the active plane without dragging, but leaves its appearance unchanged (it is not foreshortened; drag it onto the grid with this tool for that), and Move Plane to Match Object moves the plane to an object's position.
cards.script_api: app.selectTool("Perspective Selection Tool") selects the tool (verified live in the harvest); the drags themselves cannot be scripted. To put art on a plane by script: app.activeDocument.showPerspectiveGrid(), app.activeDocument.setPerspectiveActivePlane(PerspectiveGridPlaneType.LEFTPLANE), then pageItem.bringInPerspective(x, y, PerspectiveGridPlaneType.LEFTPLANE) on each item. Moving or scaling an item afterwards while keeping it in perspective has no DOM call in the harvest.

review.changes: how: Attach to Active Plane no longer reads as equal to dragging on (it does not foreshorten the art)

cards.name: Blend Mode - Color
cards.summary: Keyboard command (no default key, no toolbar or menu entry) that, judging by its name and its place among the blend-mode commands, sets the selected objects' blending mode to Color, the same as choosing Color in the Transparency panel. Color keeps the luminance of the artwork underneath and takes the hue and saturation of the selected object, so it tints what is below while keeping its light and dark detail. Not verified live: the harvest probe never reached this id.
use_for: tinting a grayscale or monochrome illustration with one colour shape on top
colouring a black-and-white texture or halftone without losing its tonal detail
quick duotone-style colour washes over vector art for posters
avoid: spot-colour print jobs: Illustrator does not blend spot colours in Color mode; convert to process or build the tint another way
pure white or black areas underneath: Color keeps their luminance, so they stay white or black and the colour barely shows there; use Multiply or Overlay for a visible wash
artwork for EPS, PDF/X-1a or older RIPs: the blend has to be flattened; check it in Window > Flattener Preview before sending
relying on the command in a pipeline: it has no default shortcut and is not verified; set the blending mode directly
cards.how: Assign a key to 'Blend Mode - Color' in Edit > Keyboard Shortcuts... (Tools list), select one or more objects, groups or layers' contents, and press the key. The same result comes from Window > Transparency > blending mode menu > Color. Use the Transparency panel's Isolate Blending on a group to keep the colour from reaching art outside the group. In CorelDRAW the nearest look is a Uniform Transparency on the top object with merge mode Color (cdrMergeColor).
cards.script_api: The batch has no invoke for this id (the selectTool probe stopped before it). Set the mode directly, as the ai_blend_mode harvest does for Color: for each item in app.activeDocument.selection, item.blendingMode = BlendModes.COLORBLEND.

review.changes: how: '(Tools set)' -> '(Tools list)' (a set in that dialog is the shortcut set, not the Tools list); avoid: flattening proof pointed at Window > Flattener Preview (Object > Flatten Transparency... flattens the art, it is not a proof); earlier adversarial pass: avoid: corrected the reason white / black areas stay untinted (Color keeps the underlying luminance; the hue comes from the top object, so 'no hue to keep' was wrong)

cards.name: Blend Mode - Color Burn
cards.summary: Keyboard command (no default key, no toolbar or menu entry) that, by its name, sets the selected objects' blending mode to Color Burn, as in the Transparency panel. Color Burn darkens the colours underneath toward the selected object's colour by raising contrast, giving deep, saturated, burnt-in shadows; a white object changes nothing. Not verified live: the harvest probe never reached this id.
use_for: rich, saturated shadows and vignettes over flat colour illustrations
burnt, aged or grunge texture overlays on posters and labels
making a colour shape punch darker into a background without going muddy grey
avoid: subtle shading: Color Burn quickly clips to near-black and oversaturates; use Multiply at a lower opacity
light pastel artwork underneath where a soft tone is wanted: the contrast jump looks harsh; use Multiply or Soft Light
jobs exported to EPS / PDF/X-1a: the blend is flattened on output; proof it in Window > Flattener Preview
relying on the command in a pipeline: no default shortcut and not verified; set the blending mode directly
cards.how: Assign a key to 'Blend Mode - Color Burn' in Edit > Keyboard Shortcuts... (Tools list), select the overlay object(s) and press the key; or pick Color Burn in the Window > Transparency panel's blending mode menu. Lower the opacity in the same panel to tame it. In CorelDRAW the nearest look is a Uniform Transparency with merge mode Burn (cdrMergeBurn).
cards.script_api: No invoke for this id in the batch (the selectTool probe stopped before it). Set the mode directly, as the ai_blend_mode harvest does for Color Burn: item.blendingMode = BlendModes.COLORBURN for each item in app.activeDocument.selection.

cards.name: Blend Mode - Darken
cards.summary: Keyboard command (no default key, no toolbar or menu entry) that, by its name, sets the selected objects' blending mode to Darken, as in the Transparency panel. Darken compares the selected object with what is underneath channel by channel and keeps the darker value, so parts of the object lighter than the background vanish and darker parts show. cards.name: Blend Mode - Difference
cards.summary: Keyboard command (no default key, no toolbar or menu entry) that, by its name, sets the selected objects' blending mode to Difference, as in the Transparency panel. Difference subtracts the darker of the two colours from the lighter one per channel: a white object inverts what is underneath, a black object changes nothing, and colours in between give strong, often psychedelic negative-like results. Not verified live: the harvest probe never reached this id.
use_for: inverted, negative-style type or shapes that flip colour where they cross other art
op-art, psychedelic and glitch poster graphics
checking alignment: two copies of the same art in Difference turn black where they match exactly
avoid: spot-colour print jobs: Illustrator does not blend spot colours in Difference mode; use process colours
brand colours that must stay exact: the result colour depends on what is underneath and is hard to predict; use Normal with a chosen colour
jobs exported to EPS / PDF/X-1a: the blend is flattened on output; proof it in Window > Flattener Preview
relying on the command in a pipeline: no default shortcut and not verified; set the blending mode directly
cards.how: Assign a key to 'Blend Mode - Difference' in Edit > Keyboard Shortcuts... (Tools list), select the object(s) and press the key; or pick Difference in the Window > Transparency panel. A white object over mixed art gives a clean inversion. In CorelDRAW the nearest look is a Uniform Transparency with merge mode Difference (cdrMergeDifference).

It does not apply any particular look itself; the result depends on the mode it lands on. Whether it wraps from the last mode back to Normal, and how it treats a mixed selection, is not known: the harvest probe never reached this id.
